title: Whole Milk 1 gal

drivers.name: Price increase (5.1%)
drivers.evidence: Historical comparison: same price level (4.56) in 2026-09-28 and 2026-10-05 saw 207→195→119 units; median x0.57 vs baseline. Noise-adjusted estimate of price impact: x0.82.

drivers.name: Post-promo dip (week after 30% off)
drivers.evidence: After 2024-10-28 promotion (30% off), the next week sold 200 units (x0.95 vs baseline). Noise-adjusted estimate: x0.95. The 2026-10-05 sale (119 units) confirms strong pull-forward.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 207.6. No events are scheduled. The price is raised 5.1% above regular (4.56 vs 4.34), which historically correlates with a 22% drop in sales. The week after a promotion (2026-10-05) sold 119 units (x0.57 vs baseline), indicating strong post-promo pull-forward. The heatwave (38°C) may boost demand, but milk is not a heat-driven product; past heat events show no consistent uplift. The classical model suggests no effect, but price increase and post-promo dip are confirmed drivers. Evidence is strong on price and recent dip, so adjust downward. Noise-adjusted price effect: x0.82. Post-promo effect: x0.95. Combined: x0.78. Shrink toward 1.0 due to limited past data at this price level. Final median multiplier: 0.82. Downside spread increases due to price sensitivity. Upward spread unchanged.

brief:
PRODUCT: Whole Milk 1 gal | category Dairy | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-10-19 to 2026-10-25 (2 weeks after the last week with sales data)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 4.56 (+5.1% vs regular price 4.34)
  planner notes: Heatwave forecast: 38°C all week

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 207.6 | 5%-95%: 133.7 - 290.1 | 10%-90%: 156.4 - 280.9

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-22% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
